articles.title: A dating or matching app still ships its compatibility scoring in the client
articles.excerpt: Swipe apps and niche matching products often compute a "compatibility" percentage before the user even hits like. Interests, deal-breakers, distance decay, activity scores, and the mysterious boost th…
articles.body: Swipe apps and niche matching products often compute a "compatibility" percentage before the user even hits like. Interests, deal-breakers, distance decay, activity scores, and the mysterious boost that puts some profiles on top — if that formula runs in JavaScript, it is public. This is not only an IP problem. It is a fairness and abuse problem. Anyone who can read the scorer can game it. What usually ships in the feed bundle Feature weights – shared hobbies, education, religion, smoking, kids, "intent" answers. Hard filters – age band, distance, gender preferences, verified-only. Soft boosts – recently active, high reply rate, subscription tier, "popularity" priors. Decay curves – how fast distance or inactivity hurts the score. Experiment flags – which users see which ranking variant.

articles.title: How to Operate Private File Uploads: Signed Downloads with Tenant Isolation
articles.excerpt: Short answer: Use a private file upload architecture in which the app assigns every e-commerce training artifact a tenant-scoped object storage key, then gives the browser separate signed upload and d…
articles.body: Short answer: Use a private file upload architecture in which the app assigns every e-commerce training artifact a tenant-scoped object storage key, then gives the browser separate signed upload and download grants. The control plane must own region, validation state, and an immutable deletion deadline; possession of an object key must never be enough to mint a download. Fail closed. That shape keeps bulky transfers away from the app while leaving authorization where it belongs. A signed URL is a temporary capability, not proof that the caller may read the file. Treating those as the same thing is how one tenant's product-photo labeling set ends up visible to another. The runbook has four states: pending , quarantined , ready , and deleting .

articles.body: Which database export method is faster: text or binary? There are plenty of performance comparisons online, but their results rarely apply directly to your environment. Hardware, database versions, data volume, and storage performance all influence the outcome. Instead of relying on someone else's benchmark, you can run a controlled comparison in your own environment. GBase Database(GBase 8s) provides two data export and import approaches: logical text export using dbexport / dbimport , and binary data transfer using onunload / onload . This guide explains how to compare both methods using four measurable criteria: export time, import time, artifact size, and verification effort. 1. Establish Four Rules for a Fair Benchmark Before running the comparison, control the test conditions.

articles.body: Delivery and field-service web apps love to show an optimized stop list the moment a driver opens the shift. That snappy UX usually means the scoring heuristic — distance, time windows, vehicle capacity, priority flags, and the little penalties that decide who gets visited first — is running in the browser. If it runs in the browser, every driver (and every competitor) can download it. This post walks through what ships, how it gets extracted, and how to harden the parts that actually matter. What typically lands in the driver bundle Open DevTools on a modern dispatch PWA and you will often find: Cost functions – travel time estimates, traffic multipliers, parking/delay constants per stop type. Constraint checks – max weight, max stops, refrigerated vs dry, skill tags for the driver.

articles.title: Why AI API Prompt Caching Misses and How to Debug It
articles.excerpt: A support bot sends the same refund policy with every question. After a deployment, the policy still looks identical in the template, but cached input drops to zero. The release added a timestamp at t…
articles.body: A support bot sends the same refund policy with every question. After a deployment, the policy still looks identical in the template, but cached input drops to zero. The release added a timestamp at the top of the system message. Every request now changes the prefix before the policy. Start with the request your provider actually receives. A cache can reuse processing for an eligible stretch of input you have sent before, and the model still generates a fresh answer. A change to the early input can make everything after it miss on an endpoint that matches prefixes. Claude prompt caching Compare the prefix on the route that missed Check the resolved model, endpoint, and workspace where relevant before comparing prompts.

articles.title: A browser CAD or floor-plan tool still ships its geometry kernel and snapping rules
articles.excerpt: Browser-based CAD and floor-plan editors have become seriously good. You can draw walls, drop in doors, get automatic room areas, and export a dimensioned plan without installing anything. Behind that…
articles.body: Browser-based CAD and floor-plan editors have become seriously good. You can draw walls, drop in doors, get automatic room areas, and export a dimensioned plan without installing anything. Behind that smooth experience is usually years of work on a geometry kernel: polygon offsetting, wall-join resolution, snapping heuristics, area rules, and the little tolerances that make a drawing "feel right". If that kernel runs in the browser, every visitor downloads it. This post looks at what exactly ships, how competitors actually lift it, and what you can realistically do about it. What a floor-plan editor really sends to the client Open the network tab on almost any web floor-plan tool and you will find one or two large bundles.

articles.excerpt: How realistic are the zero-g sports we see in sci-fi? We talk to Les Johnson, former Chief Technologist for NASA, to find out.
articles.body: Sports in space have a long and proud tradition, whether it's Alan Shepard playing golf on the moon or the crew of the ISS hosting their own version of the Summer Olympics . The future looks bright as well, with the foundation of the Space Games Federation , the self-described "first governing and sanctioning body for competitive sports played in zero or micro-gravity," co-founded by a NASA astronaut. articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 23, 2015: Blue Origin sticks 1st-ever rocket landing from space with its suborbital New Shepard rocket
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 23, 2015, a Blue Origin rocket made a historic landing after launching into suborbital space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 23, 2015, a Blue Origin rocket made a historic landing. Before this time, all rockets were single-use only — even SpaceX's rockets. Blue Origin changed the concept forever. After launching the New Shepard capsule safely into space, the rocket started heading back to Earth. It flew towards a landing pad, reignited its engine to slow down and touched down softly on the ground . This was the first successful vertical landing from space in history. The Blue Origin milestone meant that rockets could be reused for multiple missions, which saves money and reduces waste. (Image credit: Blue Origin) Why it mattered Today, SpaceX may be the most well-known for landing its Falcon 9 rocket boosters from orbit.
